question: to the Commission Piotr Müller (ECR) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 of the European Parliament and of the Council on data collection and sharing relating to short-term accommodation rental services entered into force on 20 May 2026, introducing a harmonised legal framework to make the sector more transparent throughout the European Union. Because Donald Tusk’s government has not yet drafted or implemented the relevant alignment legislation, Poland currently has no statutory regulations of its own to bring these EU measures into force. 1.
Is the Commission monitoring the delays in implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 in Poland and the current lack of legislative action on the part of the Polish authorities?

If the required national legislation is not implemented on time, does the Commission plan to initiate proceedings against Poland for failing to fulfil its obligations as a Member State (infringement procedure)?
What consequences does the Polish Government’s inaction in this area have when it comes to the coherence of the internal market and the effectiveness of data-sharing with online platforms?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) Regulation (EU) 2024/10281 (the Short-Term Rental (STR) Regulation) establishes a harmonised framework for the exchange of data between STR platforms and the competent authorities of the Member States. The data collected under the Regulation are intended to support Member States in designing appropriate and proportionate measures concerning the STR Regulation. The Regulation harmonises registration schemes and for data-sharing requirements concerning online STR platforms, where Member States decide to put in place such schemes or requirements. However, Member States remain free not to request data from platforms, for example where they do not intend to adopt legislation regulating or restricting the provision of short-term rental services. In light of the specific nature of the STR Regulation, which has been into effect since 20 May 2026, the Commission is monitoring its implementation to ensure the establishment of a harmonised and interoperable system enabling Member States' competent authorities to receive reliable and complete data while allowing platforms to comply with a single legal framework. However, the Commission has no power to require Member States that do not impose registration requirements to make use of the Regulation or to initiate infringement proceedings. That said, to promote the coherence of the internal market and ensure the effectiveness of the data-sharing framework established by the STR Regulation, the Commission continues to encourage all Member States to implement and make effective use of the Regulation.
